nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: The study used the Nadaraya-Watson (NW) estimator with a Gaussian kernel to construct the normative model. This is a kernel regression approach for local smoothing, which is a nonparametric regression method similar to LOESS. The bandwidth parameter h was selected by minimizing the leave-one-out cross-validation function for each ROI and dMRI modality.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: we represented the normative range in each ROI by an age specific weighted mean, mh, and standard deviation, σ2h, for each sex separately. To do so, we used the Nadaraya-Watson (NW) estimator with a Gaussian kernel
nm2_1_modeling_methods.location: Elad2021.pdf.md: Section 2.3 Construction of a normative model

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Three dMRI measures were used as response variables: (1) FA (fractional anisotropy) derived from DTI model using FSL's DTIFIT; (2) FAt (tissue fractional anisotropy) from the two-compartment Free-water imaging model; (3) FW (free-water fractional volume) from the same Free-water imaging model. These measures were computed for 17 white matter fiber tract ROIs from the IIT atlas v.4.1 plus a white matter skeleton average, totaling 18 ROIs.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: The harmonized data were fitted using FSL's DTIFIT to the DTI model, from which FA was derived. The data were also fitted to the two-compartments Free-water imaging model (including a free-water compartment and a tissue compartment)... the fractional volume of the free-water compartment (FW) as well as the FA of the tissue compartment (FAt) were estimated

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Age was used as the primary explanatory variable through the Nadaraya-Watson kernel regression estimator. Sex was handled by constructing separate normative models for males and females (exact matching approach rather than as an additional covariate). The normative model represents age-specific weighted mean and standard deviation for each sex separately.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: To control for confounding factors resulting from age and sex differences, we represented the normative range in each ROI by an age specific weighted mean, mh, and standard deviation, σ2h, for each sex separately.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.location: Elad2021.pdf.md: Section 2.3 Construction of a normative model
